sources.title: Robert L. Cooler, Post Pagan Period: Ava, architecture and painting
sources.note: Northern Illinois University art survey, direct full HTML. Use specific architecture and iconography; do not adopt the obsolete Tilokaguru 1672 dating or inconsistent nineteenth-century chronology.

sources.title: Jacques P. Leider, Alaungmintaya King of Myanmar (1752 to 1760)
sources.note: Aséanie 33 (2014), pp. 13 to 41. First page directly read; p. 15 full passage on the 1752 collapse and local resistance retrieved from indexed original.

sources.title: Wil O. Dijk, The Dutch in Seventeenth Century Burma
sources.note: Direct access returned 403, but indexed original returned full article with textile imports, trade offices and Martaban jars. Group with the shorter IIAS Newsletter 34 article as one work for attribution.

sources.title: Than Tun, The Royal Orders of Burma, Part II: 1649 to 1750
sources.note: Kyoto University edition (1985). Publisher indexed text and full searchable mirror https://www.scribd.com/document/119866098/The-Royal-Orders-of-Burma-A-D-1598-1885-Part-Two-A-D-1649-1750 checked. Dates and English translations as printed; prescriptive orders are not evidence that every instruction was implemented. Group all Royal Orders volumes conservatively.

sources.title: Than Tun, The Royal Orders of Burma, Part IV: 1782 to 1787
sources.note: Kyoto University edition (1986), printed p. 16, note to 6 March 1783 order; introduction p. xxv. Indexed original PDF confirms construction and 12 May 1783 move. Group with Part II.

sources.title: Christophe Munier-Gaillard, Origins of the Nyaungyan narrative painting tradition
sources.note: Arts Asiatiques 72 (2017), pp. 39 to 58, especially p. 40 note 5. Bibliography directly read; full indexed p. 40 explicitly rejects 1672 and places Tilokaguru with early seventeenth-century comparanda. Do not reverse the argument by treating the quoted earlier eighteenth-century theory as the author’s conclusion.

sources.title: Alexey Kirichenko, The itineraries of the Sīhaḷa monk Sāralaṅkā
sources.note: University of Hawai‘i Press chapter (2019), printed pp. 48 to 74, DOI 10.1515/9780824877200-004. Full PDF directly read; school subjects p. 60 and the 1783 list p. 61. Scope is late eighteenth-century Upper Burma, not universal literacy.

sources.title: Department of Traditional Medicine, Milestones of Traditional Medicine in Myanmar
sources.note: Direct full official PDF, printed p. 18. Named U Myat Tun manual and 1133 Myanmar Era date used. Some broad period headings elsewhere are inconsistent; avoid them. This is a modern institutional historical summary, not a surviving manuscript facsimile or clinical evaluation.

sources.title: Jacques P. Leider, King Alaungmintaya’s Golden Letter to King George II (7 May 1756)
sources.note: GWLB/EFEO scholarly monograph (2009), full PDF directly read. Exact Roman transliteration printed p. 123 line 2; English city-name translation p. 75. Original Burmese transcription p. 122 is image-only and was not used to invent Unicode text. Group with existing Burma Golden Letter passages.

proposedOverrides.name: Ava
proposedOverrides.summary: Ava across later Nyaungyan rule, the 1752 conquest and early Konbaung reconstruction.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Exact imported 1650 to 1783 ID, not medieval Ava 1364 to 1555. Three unchanged snapshots, 1650/1700/1715, span severe historical changes; public caveat retained. No aliases or successor overrides. Earlier burmese-kingdoms and later burma carry related but distinct map phases; shan-states is not absorbed. Selected pre-1650 inherited monuments are explicit. No supported seventeenth/eighteenth-century toilet arrangement was located, so none is invented. Royal orders are prescriptive; murals selective. Golden Letter transliteration checked directly; no invented Burmese rendering.
